source_findings.finding: The detailed proof splits the THREE-SPHERE into closed upper/lower balls A,B. The lower complement is contracted to infinity by downward translation. The upper complement is cut by explicit vertical sheets D_j; its free meridian basis follows via bicollars/HNN gluing. The punctured separating sphere supplies normal generators. This proves the group presentation, not the present Euclidean strong deformation-retraction/disjoint-annulus assertion. It cannot be quoted as proving the latter.

§4.2.4 uses square tunnels around a diagram standardized with high arcs at z=1, short vertical end segments, and crossing under-segments at z=0. A={z>0} minus tunnels retracts to a bouquet; B={z<epsilon/2} minus tunnels is simply connected; A intersection B is a plate with n holes. Its last exercise explicitly describes separate open cubes C_i with B_i removed to seal trench mouths. This is the closest source for the exact c>0 disjoint-cap claim. But the source describes the retraction geometrically rather than supplying parameter formulas, so local finite product collapses remain to be authored.

p3 attaches n copies of D2×I by annular faces to a principal region and states the resulting cover is homotopic to the complement. It does not verify strong deformation retraction, relative-open neighborhoods, or all collar compatibilities. Its claim that wedge-circle fundamental group is a direct sum of copies of Z is erroneous (it is free); do not copy that expression.

p35 explicitly says the relation needs overstrand orientation to distinguish left/right and does not need understrand orientation. This independently corroborates the review1 refinement: fixed geometric sides must not change their conjugation rule solely because the understrand orientation reverses.

zero_crossing_explicit_construction.status: Explicit deformation retraction to a finite two-dimensional spine established at proof-design level; wedge homotopy equivalence uses an existing published contractible-CW-collapse supplier. No claim yet of a literal embedded wedge strong deformation retract.
steps: Use S3={(z1,z2) in C2: |z1|²+|z2|²=1}, standard unknot K={z1=0}, and infinity p=(1,0). The explicit map (w,e^{it})↦(sqrt(1-|w|²)e^{it},w) identifies S3 minus K with open unit disk × S1, and p corresponds to (0,1). Stereographic projection from p identifies its puncture with R3 minus a round planar circle. The S1 phase around z1 is the positive-meridian factor after orienting the normal disk accordingly.

Identify the open disk with (-2,2)² by an explicit radial homeomorphism. Let r=max(|x|,|y|). On (-2,2)²×S1, contract each point with r>1 to radius 1 by H_s((x,y),u)=((1-s+s/r)(x,y),u), and fix r≤1. This is continuous at r=1, fixes the compact square, and never hits the removed (0,1). It gives an SDR onto M=([-1,1]²×S1) minus {(0,1)}.

Represent the S1 factor as [-1,1] with endpoints identified, placing its removed phase 1 at coordinate t=0. Thus M is Q minus {0}, Q=[-1,1]³, with only the t=-1 and t=1 faces identified. For v≠0 put rho=max(|v1|,|v2|,|v3|) and F_s(v)=(1-s+s/rho)v. It stays in Q minus {0}, is continuous there, fixes ∂Q pointwise, and is compatible with the t-face identifications because those faces have rho=1 and remain fixed. Therefore it descends to an explicit SDR onto Y=∂Q/(t=-1 face identified with t=1 face).

Y is a torus (the side cylinder with its ends identified) with one meridian disk attached (the identified end face). This explicit spine retains the missing sphere. For example its finite CW model has 1-cells a,b, a torus cell [a,b], and one extra 2-cell b; its first group is generated freely by a.

For the full homotopy type, collapse the attached disk D to a point using lem-cw-quotients-and-collapse-of-a-contractible-subcomplex. The quotient is (S1×[-1,1]) with both boundary circles collapsed to the SAME point, hence S2 with its two poles identified. Add an interval between those poles in S2: collapsing that contractible interval produces the same pole-identification quotient, so the same supplier gives a homotopy equivalence. Moving one endpoint of this interval to the other along a supplied meridian path gives a homotopy equivalent attachment at a single point, S2∨S1; the endpoint-moving homotopy can be constructed on the interval strip or supplied as an elementary local cell-attachment lemma. This last attachment-invariance step still needs explicit local writeup; no new geometric input about knots remains.
zero_crossing_explicit_construction.scope_note: For an arbitrary zero-crossing planar diagram, transporting from its projected Jordan curve to the round circle requires an explicit finite polygonal/planar-disk construction or the available published Jordan–Schoenflies theorem. The latter currently assumes full AC; do not silently import it into a choice-free/AC_omega claim. Prefer finite planar-code triangulation and explicit polygonal disk straightening. The formulas above prove the round-circle model directly and avoid Alexander duality/full AC.

positive_crossing_spine_design.status: Promising explicit route found in inspected Stillwell source; strong exact current Statement is NOT YET proved. No acceptance inferred from group correctness or matching Euler characteristic.
positive_crossing_spine_design.normalized_geometry: Finitely straighten underarc projections into pairwise disjoint planar polygonal arcs at z=1, separated by finite crossing boxes; place one short under-segment at z=0 in each box and use vertical joins. Choose rational rectangular tunnel radii below all finite separation distances. This is a concrete finite ambient-isotopy task requiring endpoint-compatible piecewise-linear charts; smooth roundings do not affect the topology.
positive_crossing_spine_design.target_handle_description: A meridian handlebody H with m=c one-handles, plus c disjoint 2-handles D2×I attached by their annular faces along the crossing loops. The union must model the PUNCTURED knot exterior (Euclidean infinity retained as an end). The compact S3 exterior instead has a final 3-handle or permits one redundant 2-handle cancellation; do not confuse those complexes.
required_local_product_checks: For each upper planar arc choose an explicit boundary-parallel rectangular spanning disk. Cutting the upper region along these c disks produces a ball/product. Prove the cut region is a ball by finite rectangle collapses, then reglue to give the meridian wedge and its common upper-collar access paths.

At each short lower under-segment, choose a disjoint rectangular trench box. The separate cap is a D2×I with annular attaching face. Parameterize its overlap with H as S1×(-epsilon,epsilon) and trace its oriented core through the upper chart to obtain the crossing word. Supports lie in disjoint finite crossing boxes.

Outside trench boxes, lower vertical fibers are intervals. Contract them toward the upper boundary/product collar; within each box use a rectangle-minus-tunnel radial collapse onto the upper faces plus its chosen cap disk. This contraction MUST be specified relative to the box boundary, so it pastes with the outside contraction. Merely saying product homotopies paste does not establish the claim.

Show these local collapses exhaust the exterior: no lower complementary component, outer sphere, or 3-cell may be discarded. A large enclosing box and the radial exterior collar retain the sphere at infinity; for c>0 it is represented by the dependence among all c crossing disks.

Only after this explicit relative collapse, take narrow regular collar neighborhoods: U retracting to H, V_i a disk neighborhood with annular overlap, and pairwise disjoint V_i. Verify they are open relative to Y and cover Y. The disjoint interiors of the handle cores alone do not prove relative openness of their neighborhoods.
positive_crossing_spine_design.smallest_missing_local_result: A relative rectangular-trench collapse lemma: the finite square-tunnel complement in a crossing box strongly deformation retracts, fixing its prescribed upper/side boundary, onto the meridian-region boundary plus one spanning cap disk; its annular attaching core is the meridian conjugacy word. Together with the no-crossing product collapse this yields the actual c>0 assertion. This still needs a coordinate-level construction or a complete finite simplicial collapse table.
positive_crossing_spine_design.alternative_group_only_proof: Friedl/Stillwell open-cover van Kampen computation can repair only the knot-group theorem with substantially less geometry. It must not be substituted silently for the approved richer cover/spine claim; owner has directed preserving that richer scope.
